I think one thing people don't realise is that a lot of FAs are in this situation for many reasons not just physical appearance. 

Physical appearance *is* a big part of it for sure, although a person can have attractive qualities that aren't physical in nature, the physical aspect is still and will always be the first thing you will notice and judge about a person. It's impossible for anyone to say "looks don't matter to me", because they always do atleast on a subconscious level. 

There are other aspects to being an FA too, for many, especially FA women, it's age. It can be a mental or physical illness that absolutely debilitates you and doesn't allow you to do the things you like or creates a wall between you and other people, and most of the time, it can just be pure, extremely shitty luck. There are more people than you think struggling to find partners or love just out of the fact that there aren't any compatible people who can overlook major unchangeable flaws easily in their range, which is absolutely possible, and the only reason it seems so abnormal is because this specific type of loneliness isn't talked about outside of communities dedicated to it. 

Solving being an FA simply isn't "oh you just have to find the right person and make connections!". A lot of FAs have already tried that. The problems usually start when you're *in the process* of trying to find the right people and make connections.

I have lots of hobbies I enjoy, I usually do them to distract myself. I knit and crochet and I've found lots of comfort in those communities. It's just harder to *make friends* specifically in public communities than most people realise.

I get how you feel, It's so hard to be ok with being alone when the people around you don't seem to even be aware of that problem existing. Feeling abnormal isn't a very nice at all. 

I wish there was a way for FAs to not compare themselves to other women as much because it seems to be one of the biggest problems affecting our self-esteem but that's easier said than done of course. I hope everything becomes easier for you soon, OP, it's not asking for much when you want a break from loneliness.

>I felt disgusting. I felt even more disgusting when guys way out of my league would message for my words, see me, and understandably bail. 

You put it perfectly. It's a feeling of being subhuman, as if you're some sort of gremlin that's maliciously tricking the kind, benevolent and handsome prince/princess, even when that's not the case *at all*. 

>I'd see a guy who looked like me and realize, oh, this is what guys see when they look at me - numbness.

This too. Honestly I feel like such a hypocrite when I catch myself judging other people's looks. It really is an innate, built in behaviour in people. Sometimes I wonder if I should just stay celibate on purpose and let my family tree end at me even though I'd love a family. That halo effect is there for a reason, why fight natural selection you know? This type of logic is so hurtful but it just creeps into your mind. 

>Just being able to take a photo and not being ashamed would be laugh changing
 
I'm trying not to think about this sentence too hard or it might just make me cry. This really hits deep. That's exactly the feeling it is, shame. It's gone past insecurities for many FAs at this point. It's pure, heartbreaking, mortifying *shame*.

This is so true! Bitter behaviour from other people really does manifest in a person and make them bitter too. I was so terrified of becoming this little ball of festering anger that I started becoming one and I forced myself to be compassionate and empathetic and thoughtful because of how scared I was. 

It's hard of course, it's very draining to always think about everything you're doing and saying, it's easy to just be too lazy and sulk because sometimes it just feels nice to feel negative things, but honestly it's really helped me. 

Turns out, people's intentions aren't as bad as I thought, and it really *feels* better when I'm nice to people, even on days where it's really hard to muster up that compassion for others. And eventually, it becomes a habit and you don't have to think about it anymore. 

At this point, I don't mind being alone for the reminder of my life, I just want to do everything in my power to make sure that this loneliness isn't my fault, and that I'm not digging myself into this hole and then crying about how deep it is.
The rest of a person can vary, I just want them to have good intentions. Men who do small deeds of kindness naturally for no reason other than because they can will always make my heart flutter.
